deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the opening of 'Structures stratifiées'. The page continues the elementary case of a closed subspace Y ↪ X (1) whose normal structure is locally trivial: locally X' ≅ Y' × Z, with Y' sitting as Y' × {z}. The previous page announced a 'tubular (infinitesimal) neighbourhood' factorization Y ↪ V_{Y,X} ↪ X (3), still to be defined.

This page proposes a provisional definition. For X a topological space, V_{Y,X} is the 'germ of space' of X around Y. As a topos it is the topological projective limit lim←_{U ⊇ Y} Sh(U), taken over the open neighbourhoods U of Y.

Heuristically:
- V_{Y,X} → X behaves like an open immersion, being a limit of open immersions.
- Y → V_{Y,X} behaves like a closed immersion.
- So (3) is a canonical factorization of the closed immersion (1): a closed immersion into the germ, followed by a pro-open immersion.

The marginal insertion states the key intuition: Y → V_{Y,X} should be a homotopy equivalence (4). A struck-out version derived this from normal local triviality plus 'modération' (tameness) conditions. The margin seems to say it should hold independently of local triviality, which matches the next page's 'indépendamment de toute hypothèse de locale trivialité normale'.

Motivating example:
- Y and X* = X − Y are manifolds.
- The normal slice Z has Z* = Z − {z} a manifold. Under tameness this should follow from the first hypothesis.
- z is a singular point of Z, so X is 'singular along Y'.

The programme, carried out on the next page, is to rebuild X from the manifolds Y and X* as elementary building blocks:
- Introduce the deleted germ V* = V ∩ X*.
- Present X as the pushout (recollement / topos colimit) of X* ← V* → V, where V ≃ Y homotopically.

In modern terms this is the decomposition of a two-stratum space into strata plus link data (homotopy link / deleted tubular neighbourhood). It is the germ of Grothendieck's dévissage theorem for tame stratified spaces in Esquisse d'un programme §5.
errors: Taken literally, the provisional definition degenerates. The projective limit in the 2-category of topoi of the open subtopoi Sh(U), U ⊇ Y, is their intersection as subtopoi. Equivalently it is the localic limit, the meet of the open sublocales containing Y. For fit (e.g. regular, hence metrizable) spaces, every closed sublocale is the intersection of the open sublocales containing it. Hence lim← Sh(U) = Sh(Y).

Consequences of that degeneration: V_{Y,X} is just Y, (4) becomes trivially an equivalence, and the deleted germ V* = V ∖ Y of the next page is the empty topos. The gluing then carries no information. This is consistent with tautness: H*(Y, F|Y) = colim H*(U, F) for paracompact X.

The germ must therefore be kept as a pro-object (pro-space or pro-topos, i.e. the shape of the system of neighbourhoods), not as an actual limit. Alternatively it can be replaced by a homotopy link or by an oriented-product (vanishing) topos. Grothendieck's own '(à titre provisoire !)' signals awareness that the definition is not final.

The claim that Y → V_{Y,X} is a homotopy equivalence 'without local triviality' needs tameness hypotheses. For wild closed subsets (e.g. the Warsaw circle type phenomena) neighbourhoods do not retract, and only a shape (pro-homotopy) statement survives. Grothendieck explicitly invokes 'modération' conditions in the struck text.

ideas.what: Tubular neighbourhood of a closed stratum defined as the germ (pro-system / limit topos) of open neighbourhoods, giving a canonical factorization closed immersion = closed-into-germ followed by pro-open-immersion
ideas.modern_name: germ of neighbourhoods / pro-tubular neighbourhood; homotopy link; vanishing (oriented product) topos as topos-theoretic replacement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (tubular neighbourhoods/control data); Quinn 1988 (homotopy links); Deligne/Laumon (oriented products, vanishing topos, ca. 1977–83)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 on tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures (in spirit; not this exact topos definition)

ideas.what: Inclusion of the stratum into its germ neighbourhood is a homotopy equivalence (under tameness), with or without normal local triviality
ideas.modern_name: regular neighbourhood / deformation retraction of neighbourhoods; shape-theoretic tautness
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (regular neighbourhoods), Borsuk (shape), Thom–Mather / Lojasiewicz (triangulability of tame sets)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tubular neighbourhoods of strata as homotopy-equivalent)

ideas.what: Normal local triviality along a stratum with a singular conical normal slice Z; a regular part Z* that is a manifold should follow from tameness
ideas.modern_name: locally cone-like stratified sets (CS sets), Thom–Mather stratified spaces, links

ideas.what: Programme to reconstruct X from the strata Y and X* (manifolds) as elementary building blocks via the deleted neighbourhood
ideas.modern_name: dévissage / unzipping of stratified spaces; homotopy pushout X* ← link → Y
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984), later Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping), Lurie HA Appendix A, Barwick–Glasman–Haine (exodromy)

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks a 'technically simple' topos-theoretic definition of the tubular germ V_{Y,X}, with V_{Y,X} → X open-immersion-like and Y → V closed-immersion-like. His provisional limit-topos definition collapses to Y for regular spaces. The correct topos-theoretic object is a pro-topos or an oriented product, which later literature supplied independently (vanishing topoi; links in exodromy). Nothing here appears new beyond what Esquisse §5 and later work contain.
missed.quote: on pourra prendre (à titre provisoire !) pour V_{Y,X} le "germe d'espace" de X autour de Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly of historical interest. It documents (c. 1981, before Esquisse) Grothendieck's attempt to make the dévissage of stratified spaces topos-theoretic. That anticipates the oriented-product / exodromy approach to stratified homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas (tubular germ, homotopy equivalence with the stratum, reconstruction of X by gluing strata along deleted neighbourhoods) are the familiar content of Esquisse §5 and Thom–Mather/Quinn theory. The topos framing is an early draft with a definition that, taken literally, degenerates. Its interest is historical rather than a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Si X est [-un-] [-pr...-] espace [?]' likely reads 'Si X est un espace topologique' (struck words then 'espace topologique').
'qui est tel que topos, sur le lim← topologique' should likely read 'qui est, en tant que topos, la lim← topologique des voisinages ouverts de Y dans X'.

Marginal note likely reads: 'L'intuition principale de cette factorisation est que Y → V_{Y,X} est équivalence d'homotopie (indépendamment de toute hyp. de locale trivialité)'. It is not '(i.e. dans l'hyp. de local trivialité ...)'; compare the next page's 'indépendamment de toute hypothèse de locale trivialité normale'.

Struck passage: 'L'hypothèse de locale trivialité normale implique que (moyennant des conditions de "modération" convenables) une ...' is fully struck. The surviving annotation above (4) is 'équiv. d'homotopie'.
Bottom: 'Supposons p. ex. Y et X−Y = X* des variétés, et Z* = Z∖{z} une variété ... alors que z est un pt singulier de Z' (the inserted 'de Z' is correct).
